turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung was puzzled, he thought, what use was all this, O-lan was fussing over the wedding, but what of her own health?

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan thought that the time had come to settle the eldest son, now that the house was full of noise and confusion, a wife would bring order to the household.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son was worried about his mother's health, but he tried to reassure her, telling her not to worry about him, that he would take care of himself, and that a wife would bring happiness to the household, but he urged her to take care of her own health, to get better.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: It would be a comfort to her to see the eldest son settled before she went to the other place.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung was exasperated, he thought, what use is all this fussing, O-lan? She was not well, and yet she worried about settling the son, and now about the wedding. She must think of her own health, not of others.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan thought that a wife would bring happiness to the eldest son, and peace to the household, yes, peace.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son was content to take care of himself, but he knew a wife would bring joy to their household, just as O-lan had always done.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Wang Lung would know, he has always been one to worry about the household, now it is his turn to think of the eldest son's happiness, and a wife would bring that happiness, yes, it would.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: How can she think of such things now, O-lan, when she should be thinking of her own recovery?

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son was calm, he told Wang Lung, that O-lan would rest and recover, and then they would find a good wife for him, he was sure of it.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung was dead set against O-lan's worrying about their son's future, he thought, and it was not for him to decide who would bring happiness to their son, but he would see to it that it was done, and soon.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Wang Lung would know, he has always been one to worry about the household, now it is his turn to think of the eldest son's happiness, and a wife would bring that happiness, yes, it would

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son was young and strong, he reassured O-lan and Wang Lung, and he would find a good wife when the time was right, but for now, they should focus on Wang Lung's recovery.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: How can she be so foolish, O-lan, when she should be thinking of her own life?

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Wang Lung knows, he has always thought of the household's well-being, now it is time for him to think of the eldest son's future, a good wife will bring him happiness, yes, it will

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He must be patient, Mother, he said gently, and not worry about his future, for he will find a good wife when the time is right, and not before.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid spoke softly, her eyes downcast, Mother, you should rest, it is not good for you to talk so much, and the eldest son will find a good wife when the time is right, just as he said.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He would take care of his mother, and help Wang Lung with the household chores, so that they could all focus on finding a good wife for him.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: Wang Lung must make sure the eldest son finds a good wife, it is the only way he will be happy, yes, a good wife is like a garden, she needs to be tended and nurtured

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: He is confident that with Mother's guidance and Father's support, he will find a good wife, someone who will make them all happy and bring joy to the household.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
